meta.design: v1 "square native" in code (tag design-v1-square-native, checked against v2.7.0 source on 2026-11-07); v2 decisions adopted in this system

tokens.name: background
tokens.usage: Window, menu bar, status strip and the fill behind labels. The ground for `text`, `secondary` and `accent`.

tokens.name: panel
tokens.usage: Neutral button fill; unselected Linux tabs. `text` and `secondary` read on it.

tokens.name: input
tokens.usage: Edits, lists, the profile sidebar and the overlay preview's ground.

tokens.name: border
tokens.usage: 1 px outline of enabled Windows controls: 3.2:1 on `background`, 3.5:1 on `input`. On a `panel` button it reads 2.7:1 against its own fill; the button's edge against `background` carries the 3:1.

tokens.name: divider
tokens.usage: Disabled control outlines and the menu-bar and status-strip lines. Decorative only (1.3:1 on `background`): never the only edge of something that can be clicked.

tokens.name: text
tokens.usage: Primary text on `background`, `panel`, `input`, `button_hover`, `row_hover`, `pressed` and `selection` (at least 9.7:1 on each).

tokens.name: secondary
tokens.usage: Labels, status text, "Off" tags and executable names, on `background`, `input`, `panel` and `selection` (at least 5.4:1). Above `subtext` and `verbose` in the text ladder.

tokens.name: subtext
tokens.usage: Hints beside or under a field ("0 = off", the drag hint, why a button is disabled): 6.5:1 on `background`, 7.1:1 on `input`, 5.5:1 on `panel`. Not on selected rows (4.3:1 at worst); never smaller than the body size.

tokens.name: verbose
tokens.usage: Diagnostics and trace lines, always in `win-mono` / `linux-mono` so the face sets them apart from `subtext`: 5.9:1 on `background`, 6.4:1 on `input`, 4.9:1 on `panel`. Not on selected rows.

tokens.name: disabled
tokens.usage: Disabled text and glyphs only. Appearance refuses an override below 3:1 against the role's fill; the defaults give 4.2:1 on `background` and 3.5:1 on `panel`.

tokens.name: button_hover
tokens.usage: Neutral button, menu-bar item and check box fill under the pointer (a check box's outline turns `text` too).

tokens.name: row_hover
tokens.usage: List row, drop-down and edit-role hover fill, and an open drop-down.

tokens.name: pressed
tokens.usage: Neutral button fill while pressed.

tokens.name: accent
tokens.usage: The one accent: primary button fill, selection rail, focus ring and edge, checked boxes. Never decorative. At least 4.7:1 on `background`, `input` and `panel` in every preset.

tokens.name: on_accent
tokens.usage: Text and the check tick on an `accent` fill: #141414 when the accent's luma (299R + 587G + 114B) is at least 140000, else white. Every preset lands on #141414 (6.3:1 or more).

tokens.name: selection
tokens.usage: Selected list row, selected Linux tab: `background` blended 60/255 toward `accent`. `text` reads 9.7:1 or more on it; list rows add a 3 px `accent` rail.

tokens.name: primary_hover
tokens.usage: Primary button, and a checked check box, under the pointer: `accent` blended 40/255 toward `text`. `on_accent` stays the label.

tokens.name: primary_pressed
tokens.usage: Primary button while pressed: `accent` blended 60/255 toward the button's fill (`panel`), as `paint_native_button` does. `on_accent` stays the label, 4.6:1 or more.

tokens.name: yes
tokens.usage: Worked or healthy (LayerD running, validation passed, saved), always with a ✓ or a word: 9.9:1 on `background`, 10.7:1 on `input`, 8.3:1 on `panel`, 6.4:1 or more on `selection`. Text and glyphs only, never a control fill.

tokens.name: no
tokens.usage: Failed or stopped (LayerD not running, rule errors, capability faults), always with a ✕ or a word: 5.4:1 on `background`, 5.9:1 on `input`, 4.5:1 on `panel`. On a selected row (3.5:1 at worst) only the glyph keeps this color and the message turns `text`. Same lightness as Copper's accent, so never rely on hue.

tokens.name: warning
tokens.usage: Works but needs a look (low overlay contrast, unsaved draft, degraded XWayland), always with a ! or a word: 11.8:1 on `background`, 12.8:1 on `input`, 9.9:1 on `panel`, 7.7:1 or more on `selection`.

tokens.name: on_status
tokens.usage: Text on a `yes`, `no` or `warning` fill (a badge or pip): 6.0:1 on `no`, 11.0:1 on `yes`, 13.2:1 on `warning`. Fixed rather than the `on_accent` luma rule, which would put white on `no` (3.1:1).

tokens.name: accent_2
tokens.usage: The secondary color: information that is neither good nor bad (in progress such as "connecting", notes, links). Blue in the Copper and Plum presets, violet in Teal and Slate, so its hue never matches the accent. 7.2:1 on `background`, 6.0:1 on `panel`, 4.7:1 or more on `selection`. Text and glyphs only; it never marks focus, selection or the primary action.

tokens.name: preset-copper
tokens.usage: Graphite / Copper's accent as a fixed value, for showing presets side by side (Appearance swatches, the cover). In UI, use `accent`. The default preset on both platforms.

tokens.name: preset-teal
tokens.usage: Graphite / Teal's accent as a fixed value, for showing presets side by side (Appearance swatches, the cover). In UI, use `accent`.

tokens.name: preset-plum
tokens.usage: Graphite / Plum's accent as a fixed value, for showing presets side by side (Appearance swatches, the cover). In UI, use `accent`.

tokens.name: preset-slate
tokens.usage: Graphite / Slate's accent as a fixed value, for showing presets side by side (Appearance swatches, the cover). In UI, use `accent`. Called `dark` in code.

tokens.name: linux-outline-background
tokens.usage: Linux outline on a `background` fill: `control_border` blends the fill 91/255 toward white, which lands exactly on Windows' `border`. 3.2:1 on `background`. The shipped code still blends 84/255 (#686868, 3.0:1). A disabled control's outline fades halfway into its fill and needs no minimum.

tokens.name: linux-outline-panel
tokens.usage: Linux outline on a `panel` fill (buttons, unselected tabs): 3.1:1 on `panel` at 91/255. An edit's outline on `input` is #696969, 3.3:1. (Shipped at 84/255: #727272, 2.9:1.)

groups.name: Windows
groups.note: The system message font (NONCLIENTMETRICS.lfMessageFont, normally Segoe UI) at 96 DPI, scaled by DPI and Options > Text size (100/115/130 %).

styles.name: win-heading
styles.usage: Section headings: the body face, semibold.

styles.name: win-body
styles.usage: All other text: 9 pt at 96 DPI.

styles.name: win-mono
styles.usage: Monospace at body size: Cascadia Mono, else Consolas.

groups.name: Linux
groups.note: The XSETTINGS Gtk/FontName family, else fontconfig sans; forms are authored at 14 px. A desktop size of 11–14 px sets the text size, smaller stays 11 px, and above 14 px the text stays 14 px while FLTK's screen scale grows by size / 14. FLTK's own screen scaling multiplies in.

styles.name: linux-heading
styles.usage: Headings: FLTK bold of the same face.

styles.name: linux-body
styles.usage: Body text at the authored size, the LayerD status pane included. A desktop size of 11–13 px brings it down; above 14 px the screen scale grows instead.

spacing.note: One 8 px rhythm per platform. Windows values are 96-DPI logical pixels, scaled by DPI and text size.

tokens.name: win-gap-dialog
tokens.usage: Windows: between controls in dialogs, and the gap that makes the row pitch (control + 8). In code: `DialogLayout` and `editor_layout.cpp`.

tokens.name: win-margin
tokens.usage: Windows: main window and dialog margin. In code: `DialogLayout` and `editor_layout.cpp`.

tokens.name: win-gap-main
tokens.usage: Windows: between groups in the main window. In code: `DialogLayout` and `editor_layout.cpp`.

tokens.name: win-section-gap
tokens.usage: Windows: between groups in the profile column (Timing and key, Overlay bar, Visual trigger). In code: `section_gap` (`editor_layout.cpp`).

tokens.name: swatch-inset
tokens.usage: Inset of the 16 px swatch inside a color button.

tokens.name: linux-group-gap
tokens.usage: Linux: the smallest gap between groups; forms use 10–15 px.

tokens.name: linux-margin
tokens.usage: Linux: outer margin of the main window and dialogs, and the largest gap between groups.

radius.note: Square everywhere. Only radio buttons are round, because roundness is their meaning.

tokens.name: radius-none
tokens.usage: Every control, focus ring and window frame (Windows sets DWMWCP_DONOTROUND).

tokens.name: radius-radio
tokens.usage: Radio buttons and their dot, nothing else.

size.note: Control metrics and layout constants. Windows values are 96-DPI logical pixels.

tokens.name: outline
tokens.usage: Every control outline, on both platforms.

tokens.name: focus-width
tokens.usage: 2 px focus on both platforms (`paint_focus_ring`): an `accent` ring inside the edge of the focused button, edit, drop-down, list row, tab or check box (around box and label); on the primary button the ring is `text`. On edits and drop-downs it replaces the 1 px outline. A focused list takes a 2 px `accent` bottom edge and rings its focused row.

tokens.name: accent-rail
tokens.usage: The `accent` rail on a selected list row, and the bar along the top of the selected Linux tab.

tokens.name: checkbox
tokens.usage: Check box and radio size (`native_check_box_size`); the label starts 8 px after it, and the whole width is the click area.

tokens.name: swatch
tokens.usage: The square swatch in a color button.

tokens.name: win-control-height
tokens.usage: Windows native_control_height: every button and edit. Drop-downs are `win-combo-height`. In code: `native_control_height` (`dialog_layout.hpp`).

tokens.name: win-combo-height
tokens.usage: Windows drop-downs: a drop-down list's height is set by Windows from the font, so layout code can't change it; 23 px with the 12 px body font.

tokens.name: win-row-pitch
tokens.usage: Windows: one form row (control height + 8). In code: `DialogLayout` (`dialog_layout.hpp`).

tokens.name: win-list-row
tokens.usage: Windows: one row in an item list (cooldowns, panel items, control roles). Measured from screenshots; not named in the source document.

tokens.name: win-profile-row
tokens.usage: Windows: one row in the profile list. Measured from screenshots; not named in the source document.

tokens.name: win-heading-pitch
tokens.usage: Windows: a section heading's row. In code: `DialogLayout` (`dialog_layout.hpp`).

tokens.name: win-chevron-zone
tokens.usage: Windows: the drop-down's chevron zone at its right. In code: `paint_flat_combo` (`native_controls.cpp`).

tokens.name: win-status-strip
tokens.usage: Windows: status strip height at the bottom of the main window. In code: `editor_layout.cpp`.

tokens.name: win-sidebar-min
tokens.usage: Windows: profile sidebar width is clamp(width / 5, 200, 280). In code: `editor_layout.cpp`.

tokens.name: win-sidebar-max
tokens.usage: Windows: the sidebar's widest. In code: `editor_layout.cpp`.

tokens.name: win-preview-from
tokens.usage: Windows: the preview corner shows from this window width, as wide as slot 3; below it the settings slots stack. In code: `editor_layout.cpp`.

tokens.name: win-slot-min
tokens.usage: Windows main window: the narrowest a settings slot gets; below it slots 1 and 2 stack in one column. See the Layout page.

tokens.name: win-field-cap
tokens.usage: Windows: the widest a field grows. In code: `editor_layout.cpp`.

tokens.name: win-timing-label
tokens.usage: Windows: the timing label's width. In code: `editor_layout.cpp`.

tokens.name: linux-input-height
tokens.usage: Linux: edits and choices (fixed FLTK forms). In code: fixed coordinates in `editor_forms.cpp` and the dialogs.

tokens.name: linux-button-height
tokens.usage: Linux: buttons. In code: fixed coordinates in `editor_forms.cpp` and the dialogs.

tokens.name: linux-sidebar
tokens.usage: Linux: profiles list and sidebar panes. In code: `editor_forms.cpp`.

tokens.name: linux-window-width
tokens.usage: Linux main window width; it fits without scrolling. In code: `editor_forms.cpp`.

tokens.name: linux-window-height
tokens.usage: Linux main window height; smaller windows scroll rather than overlap. In code: `editor_forms.cpp`.
